samples.summary: The new `watch()` try/catch around `doc.subscribe` — the entire point of this delta's provider change — has no test where `subscribe` throws
samples.evidence: The delta wraps both subscriptions because `subscribe` throws `YorkieError(ErrInvalidArgument, 'Unsupported event type')` on SDK versions that don't know these events, and a throw out of the effect would take down the editor subtree. Both suites that exercise `DurableLossWatch` use fake docs whose `subscribe` accepts any event name and never throws: `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx:74-81` (`subscribe: (type, cb) => { handlers.set(...); return () => ... }`) and `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:55-65`. So the guarded path is never executed — deleting the try/catch (or catching the wrong thing) leaves every test green while the real failure it exists for (the whole collaborative document unmounting on an older SDK) ships undetected. There is also no test that when the first subscription throws the second is still attempted, and that the already-registered unsubscribers are still collected/cleaned up.

samples.summary: `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` changed from swallow-and-return-0 to propagating the failure, and no unit test pins the new contract
samples.evidence: The delta removes the `catch { console.warn(...); return 0; }` from `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` so the caller's recovery gate can distinguish 'reconciled' from 'failed'. `packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-erase.test.ts` (the `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` describe block, lines ~460-551) has no case where `storedDocumentIds`/`purgeDocument` fails; every assertion is on a resolved count. Nothing fails if someone restores the swallow — and if it is restored, the runtime gate opens on a reconcile that never happened, which is exactly the harm (offering an archive from a workspace the user was removed from) the change exists to prevent. The runtime-level test 'offers nothing back when the purge itself failed' mocks `@/lib/offline-erase` wholesale (offline-runtime.test.tsx:20-28), so it cannot cover the real function. Also untested: that `store.close()` in the `finally` still runs on the throwing path.

samples.summary: No test that an unreadable/refused document skips only that item — every offer test uses a single-item work list, so `continue` vs `return` is unpinned
samples.evidence: `offerRecoverableWork` iterates all recoverable items and the new error handler uses `continue` so one 403/network failure does not abandon the remaining archives. Every test in offline-runtime.test.tsx seeds `listRecoverableWork.mockResolvedValue([{ id: 1, docKey: 'sheet-7' }])` — one item (lines 236, 255, 271, 283, 292, 299, 313, 329). Changing `continue` to `return` (or to `break`) would keep all tests green while silently withholding every other piece of unsaved work behind the first unreadable one.

samples.summary: The 404 test asserts only that a toast appeared; it does not check that the fallbacks it exists for actually travel to recovery
samples.evidence: 'still offers work whose document was deleted upstream' (lines 279-287) sets `fetchDocument` to reject with a 404 and asserts `toastWarning` was called. The behavior the 404 branch is for — keeping `title = 'Untitled'` and `workspaceId = undefined` so recovery uses the user's first workspace — is not asserted: neither the toast description nor the `recoverOfflineCopy` arguments are inspected. A regression that, say, left `title` as a stale value or passed a wrong workspace would still pass this test.

verdict.reason: The try/catch added around both `doc.subscribe` calls in DurableLossWatch (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:268-307) has no test that exercises it. Only two suites mount DurableLossWatch, and every fake doc they supply has a non-throwing `subscribe`: durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx:70-86 (map-backed, accepts any event name), collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:53-66 (pushes the event name, returns a splicing unsubscriber), and collab-document-provider-identity.test.tsx:31 (`subscribe: () => () => {}`). collab-document-provider.test.tsx has no `subscribe` on its fakeDoc at all; its `not.toThrow` cases (:145,:187,:202) concern presence writes/`doc.update`. Repo-wide greps for `Unsupported event|ErrInvalidArgument|could not watch|durability event` hit only the source comment/log, and a multiline `subscribe...throw` scan over all test files turns up only unrelated `session.subscribe` cases in packages/notes and packages/debug-report. So the guarded path — and the follow-on behavior that a throw from the first subscription still lets the second be attempted and already-collected unsubscribers be cleaned up — is never executed; removing or mis-scoping the catch leaves every test green while an older SDK would unmount the whole editor subtree. Missing test over a user-visible failure the delta exists to prevent: major under the test-adequacy rubric.

finding.evidence: The delta removes the `catch { console.warn(...); return 0; }` from `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` so the caller's recovery gate can distinguish 'reconciled' from 'failed'. `packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-erase.test.ts` (the `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` describe block, lines ~460-551) has no case where `storedDocumentIds`/`purgeDocument` fails; every assertion is on a resolved count. The runtime-level test 'offers nothing back when the purge itself failed' mocks `@/lib/offline-erase` wholesale (offline-runtime.test.tsx:20-28), so it cannot cover the real function. verdict.reason: The finding is accurate. `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` (offline-erase.ts:452-494) has only `try/finally` with no `catch`, and its docstring (lines 443-451) makes throwing-on-failure the explicit contract that the caller's recovery gate depends on. The only tests over the real (unmocked) function are in offline-erase.test.ts's `describe("access somebody else ended")` block (lines 457-552); all six cases assert resolved counts/post-state, and a grep for `rejects|toThrow|mockRejected` in that file hits only lines 97-431, all in the eraseOfflineData/logout/retry blocks via `dropAllForUser`. No case makes `storedDocumentIds` or `purgeDocument` fail, so restoring a swallow-and-return-0 breaks no test. I searched wider for a counterexample: only 5 files mention the symbol; workspaces.ts:151 is prose; offline-runtime.test.tsx mocks `@/lib/offline-erase` wholesale at lines 20-28, so its 'offers nothing back when the purge itself failed' case (248-261) drives a fabricated `mockRejectedValue` at line 254 and tests only the caller's gate, never the real function's contract. tests/api/auth.test.ts:87 also mocks the module. No e2e/integration path reaches the real implementation. The `store.close()` in the `finally` on the throwing path is likewise unexercised. Blocking at major under the test-adequacy rubric: a changed behavior with no meaningful test, whose silent regression would open the recovery gate on a reconcile that never happened and offer back an archive from a workspace the user was removed from.

finding.summary: The housekeeping store's `userId` is recorded by the test harness and never asserted — nothing pins the scope that archive recovery reads under
finding.evidence: `offline-runtime.test.tsx:32` declares `const constructed: Array<{ userId: string }> = []`, line 37 pushes the constructor options into it, and line 96 clears it in `beforeEach` — but no `expect` in the file ever reads `constructed` (grep for `constructed` in that file returns only lines 32, 37 and 96). The `WafflebaseDocStore` this runtime builds is what `listRecoverableWork` and `recoverOfflineCopy` run against, and `WafflebaseDocStore.listArchives()`/`loadArchive()` scope purely on that `userId`. If `OfflineRuntime` constructed it with the wrong identity (or a stale one after the `userId` prop changed), the session would be offered another account's archived documents back and could materialise them as new documents it owns — exactly the cross-account leak `wafflebase-doc-store-archive.test.ts` is careful about at the store layer. The harness already captures the value; one `expect(constructed[0]).toEqual({ userId: '42', isOpenElsewhere: expect.any(Function) })` would close it.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no `expect` in offline-runtime.test.tsx ever reads the captured `constructed` store options, leaving the housekeeping store's `userId` scope unpinned. That is false in the working tree. Line 136-145 is a dedicated test, 'scopes the housekeeping store to the signed-in user', which renders `<OfflineRuntime userId="42" />`, waits for construction, and asserts `expect(constructed[0].userId).toBe('42')` — precisely the assertion the finding proposes as the fix. A second test at 147-160 reads `constructed[0].isOpenElsewhere`, invokes it, and asserts it delegates as `isOpenInAnyTab('pk/wb:1:sheet-7/sheet-7', { userId: '42', whenUnknown: false })`, pinning the identity on the store's other capability too. The store mock at 38-46 captures the real constructor options passed by offline-runtime.tsx:78-81 (`new WafflebaseDocStore({ userId, isOpenElsewhere })`), so a wrong or absent id would fail these assertions. The finding's cited line numbers (32/37/96) do not correspond to the current file (36/41/107), and the grep result it reports is contradicted by the reads at lines 143, 144, 152, 153.
